title: Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that (1 - beta) log q >= c for an absolute constant c > 0 and every real zero beta of every primitive real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q >= 3, the logarithmic form of the Landau–Siegel problem. The prime bias forced by a real zero near 1, an interpolation theorem for polynomials with separately bounded degrees on a projected integer box, a weighted determinant of conjugates in Q(sqrt d, sqrt 2), and its two bounds: Hadamard's inequality, and divisibility by the Frobenius congruence at the primes with chi(p) = -1. A zero-free region with no exceptional zero follows.

units.title: Real zeros and the prime bias

prerequisites: complex analysis and Dirichlet L-functions as in the programme courses The Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions, cited at each use
linear algebra over a field: determinants, rank, Hadamard's inequality
